reconcile.note: Henry distinguishes a slavish, punishment-driven fear from the filial, reverential fear that Scripture commands, so the New Testament casts out only the former.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible ("Should we fear God?") (2013).

sides.snippet: You shall fear Yahweh your God; and him shall you serve, and shall swear by his name.
sides.verseText: You shall fear Yahweh your God; and him shall you serve, and shall swear by his name.

sides.snippet: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear, because fear has punishment. He who fears is not made perfect in love.
sides.verseText: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear, because fear has punishment. He who fears is not made perfect in love.
